from.place: Proof paragraph 2, finite-coefficient mapping-complex adjunction infrastructure reached through lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints; HTT Proposition 5.4.4.3, used in the pushout and two-out-of-three parts of Lemma 5.5.4.14 to express diagrams in an accessible functor category as filtered colimits of small compact diagrams. General tool: Filtered coherent sections and cofinal evaluation.

title: Filtered coherent sections and cofinal evaluation
statement: Use the universes, smallness, compactness and filteredness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and the coherent functors, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Use cocartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], with the same horn and edge lifting conditions over arbitrary simplicial bases. Let $\lambda<\kappa$ be infinite regular cardinals, with $\kappa$ uncountable and $\mu^\nu<\kappa$ for all $\mu<\kappa$ and $\nu<\lambda$. Let $X$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set and let $q:Y\to X$ be a cocartesian fibration. Suppose every fiber $Y_x$ is $\kappa$-filtered and admits colimits of every $\kappa$-small $\lambda$-filtered diagram, and every edge transport $Y_x\to Y_{x\prime}$ preserves these colimits. Then the quasicategory $\Gamma(q)=\operatorname{Fun}_{/X}(X,Y)$ of all sections is $\kappa$-filtered. For every vertex $x\in X$, evaluation $\Gamma(q)\to Y_x$ is cofinal: for every $y\in Y_x$, the coherent comma category of pairs $(s,y\to s(x))$ is weakly contractible. No bound on the size of the total space Y or of its fibers beyond the fixed larger universe is imposed, and sections are not required to preserve cocartesian edges.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.4.2, printed pp. 432-434; its hypotheses (i)-(iv), both conclusions (1)-(2), and the comma-category argument in its proof. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this coherent section theorem.

proof.text: We first record the small horn-completion construction used below. If $H$ is $\kappa$-small and $H\to C$ maps into a quasicategory, attach one $\Delta^n$ along each inner horn $\Lambda_i^n\to H$, choosing its image in $C$ by the horn-filling property. Repeat countably and take the union. The result $H\hookrightarrow\widehat H\to C$ has $\widehat H$ a quasicategory, and the inclusion has the left lifting property against every inner fibration: solve successive horn lifts and take their unions. It is a categorical equivalence by the lifting/model classes of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. It adds no vertices. At each round there are fewer than $\kappa$ finite horn diagrams; the countable union remains $\kappa$-small because $\kappa$ is uncountable regular, using the smallness convention of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. All choices concern the small source, not a bounded subcategory of $C$.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, opening reduction via 5.4.1.2 and the completion of K(α) at successor stages; read online, not archived

proof.text: Apply Step 1 to $X\to *$, obtaining the $\kappa$-small inner-horn completion $i:X\hookrightarrow X'$. The cocartesian dual of clause (2) of [lem-coef-cartesian-base-equivalence-invariance] gives $q':Y'\to X'$ and a cocartesian-edge-preserving comparison $u:Y\to i^*Y'$ over $X$. All of its conditional model and Quillen hypotheses in the containing universe are supplied by [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model]; its fiberwise criterion and marked inverse clause give a marked inverse to $u$. Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-horn-completion-comparison] to this $i,u,q,q'$. Its all-section equivalences commute with evaluation up to coherent natural equivalence and identify the vertex fibers. Taking its indexing shapes to be the $\kappa$-small $\lambda$-filtered quasicategories transfers the assumed fiber colimits and preservation to every edge of $X'$, including new edges. Fiber filteredness transfers by composing diagrams and cocones with inverse fiber equivalences. We may therefore work over $X'$; the displayed section equivalences will transfer the conclusions back at the end. Rename $X'$ and $Y'$ as $X$ and $Y$.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, opening paragraph, with 3.3.1.2; 2.3.2.4 for the explicitly expanded section comparison; read online, not archived

proof.text: We prove the following extension property, from which both conclusions will follow: every map $f:K\to Y$ with $K$ $\kappa$-small extends over $T(K)=K\star_X X$, with its structural map to $X$ and its original restriction on $K$. The relative join and its functoriality are [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]; put $a=qf$. By Step 1 enlarge $K$ over $Y$ to a $\kappa$-small quasicategory $K_0$. It suffices to construct the extension after this enlargement, since $T(K)\to T(K_0)$ restricts to the given map on $K$. We inductively construct monomorphisms of $\kappa$-small quasicategories over $Y$, $K_\alpha\hookrightarrow K_{\alpha+1}$ for $\alpha<\lambda$. At a nonzero limit stage $\beta<\lambda$, take the union; every finite inner horn lies in some earlier quasicategory and therefore has a filler in that union. This also describes the final union at $\lambda$.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, construction of T(K), enlargement of K, and transfinite sequence; read online, not archived

proof.text: Suppose $f_\alpha:K_\alpha\to Y$ is constructed. For each vertex $x$ and representative $\phi:A\to B_x=K_\alpha\times_X X_{/x}$ with $A$ $\lambda$-small, take the induced diagram in $X_{/x}\times_X Y$. The slice is a quasicategory by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. The cocartesian pullback assertion of [lem-coef-marked-relative-cartesian-model] makes its projection a cocartesian fibration with the given $\kappa$-filtered fibers. Appending repetitions of the final vertex $x$ supplies the prescribed cone $A^{\triangleright}\to X_{/x}$ ending at $1_x$. Apply [lem-coef-filtered-fiber-small-cone-lifting] with $\rho=\kappa$ (since $\lambda<\kappa$) to lift that cone. Each $B_x$ is $\kappa$-small: its simplices are pairs from the $\kappa$-small source and the shifted simplices of $X$, and $\kappa$ is uncountable regular. There are fewer than $\kappa$ vertices $x$. By [lem-coef-small-simplicial-diagram-cardinality] choose all representatives with $\kappa$-small coproduct of their cones. Attach those cones to $K_\alpha$ along $A$ using their projections to $Y$. The pushout is $\kappa$-small and contains $K_\alpha$ as a simplicial subset, since each $A\hookrightarrow A^{\triangleright}$ is degreewise injective. Apply Step 1 to its map into $Y$ to obtain $K_{\alpha+1}$. The attached slice components give cones in $K_{\alpha+1}\times_X X_{/x}$ extending each representative; precomposition by its isomorphism of domains covers every original diagram.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, successor stage and the count of S using the cardinal hypotheses; read online, not archived

proof.text: Let $K_\infty=\bigcup_{\alpha<\lambda}K_\alpha$ and $f_\infty:K_\infty\to Y$ be the union. Since $\lambda<\kappa$ and $\kappa$ is regular, $K_\infty$ is $\kappa$-small. It is a quasicategory by the finite-horn argument in Step 3. Each $L_x=K_\infty\times_X X_{/x}$ is a quasicategory because its projection to $K_\infty$ is the pullback of the right fibration of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; horn lifting is preserved by degreewise pullback. Its total simplices number less than $\kappa$. For any $\lambda$-small $A$ and $A\to L_x$, the component into $K_\infty$ factors through a single $K_\alpha$: fewer than $\lambda$ nondegenerate simplices have been specified, their images occur at fewer than $\lambda$ stages, and regularity of $\lambda$ bounds these stages below $\lambda$. The given slice component then gives $A\to K_\alpha\times_X X_{/x}$. Step 4 supplies a cone at stage $\alpha+1$, which lies in $L_x$. This includes the empty $A$ and proves $\lambda$-filteredness exactly as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category].

source.place: 5.4.4.2, final paragraph: smallness and filteredness of K′ ×_X X_{/x}; read online, not archived

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-relative-cylinder-extension] to $K_\infty\to X$, $q:Y\to X$ and $f_\infty$. For every $x$, its shape $L_x$ is $\kappa$-small and $\lambda$-filtered by Step 5. Every fiber $Y_z$ admits all such colimits and every transport preserves them, by the assumed colimit existence and transport preservation for $q$; thus all pairs $(x,z)$ in the cited lemma are covered. It produces $F_\infty:T(K_\infty)\to Y$ over $X$, agreeing exactly with $f_\infty$. Restrict along the relative-join map $T(K)\to T(K_\infty)$ from [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. We obtain $F:T(K)\to Y$ over $X$ with $F|_K=f$. This proves the extension property of Step 3, with no bound on $Y$.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, final extension using 4.3.2.13 and 4.3.1.11; read online, not archived

proof.text: Let $Z$ be $\kappa$-small and $d:Z\to\Gamma(q)$ be a diagram. By the definition of sections, it corresponds to $f:Z\times X\to Y$ over $X$. Its domain is $\kappa$-small: both factors have fewer than $\kappa$ total simplices and $\kappa$ is uncountable regular. Apply the extension property to this $f$. There is a simplicial map $Z^{\triangleright}\times X\to T(Z\times X)$ over $X$: on an $n$-simplex, take the initial block of vertices belonging to $Z$ as its map into $Z\times X$ and retain the entire $X$ simplex; the final cone block supplies the parameter in $\Delta^1$. The relative-join formula of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] gives precisely these data, including empty blocks. Composition with $F$ and currying gives a cone $Z^{\triangleright}\to\Gamma(q)$ extending $d$, with apex the section $F|_X$. Its induced coherent cocone is obtained using the map $Z\times\Delta^1\to Z^{\triangleright}$, which collapses the last end to the cone vertex. For $Z=\varnothing$ the same construction yields a section. By [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], $\Gamma(q)$ is $\kappa$-filtered.

source.place: 5.4.4.2, first specialization K=Z × X; read online, not archived

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$, $y\in Y_x$ and a $\kappa$-small diagram $Z\to(y\downarrow\operatorname{ev}_x)$. Its data are $f:Z\times X\to Y$ over $X$ and a cylinder $h:Z\times\Delta^1\to Y_x$, constantly $y$ at its first end and $f(-,x)$ at its second. Form $C_Z$ and $K=(Z\times X)\amalg_Z C_Z$ as in [lem-coef-relative-join-fixed-source-prism]. The maps $f,h,y$ agree on the gluing and give $K\to Y$ over $X$. This $K$ is $\kappa$-small by the degreewise pushout formula and uncountable regularity of $\kappa$, including $Z=\varnothing$. Step 6 extends it to $F:T(K)\to Y$; write $s_*=F|_X$. The cited prism gives $P:Z^{\triangleright}\times X\to T(K)$ and $J:Z^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^1\to T(K)$. Its exact restrictions say that $FP$ curries to a section cone, and $FJ$ is an arrow from the constant $y$ to its evaluation at $x$, restricting to the given $h$. Thus together they define an exact cone $Z^{\triangleright}\to(y\downarrow\operatorname{ev}_x)$ on the original diagram. Its apex is $(s_*,\beta)$, where $\beta$ is the image of the edge from the $y$ vertex of $K$ to the final $x$ vertex. The fixed-source and every higher compatibility condition follow from the stated exact restrictions, rather than a vertex-only cone.

source.place: HTT 5.4.4.2, second specialization; the fixed-source prism from returned Step 8 is now a separate statement-only input; read online, not archived

proof.text: The exact arrow comma used in Step 8 is a quasicategory. Indeed [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to $\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ and $Y_x\to *$, makes endpoint evaluation $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Y_x)\to Y_x\times Y_x$ an isofibration. Its pullback along $(y,\operatorname{ev}_x):\Gamma(q)\to Y_x\times Y_x$ is that comma, so [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-pullback-limit] applies. Both factors in this map are quasicategories, by Step 2 and the fiber hypothesis. Step 8 supplies a cone for every $\kappa$-small shape, including the empty one, so the comma is $\kappa$-filtered by [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Choose a universe containing the whole comma category. The assertion in [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] that every small filtered quasicategory is weakly contractible now proves the required contractibility for the completed base.

source.place: HTT 5.4.4.2, second specialization and filtered weak contractibility; read online, not archived

proof.text: Return to the original base using the equivalences and evaluation squares of Step 2. Section filteredness transfers by composing diagrams and cocones with the quasi-inverse section equivalences. For a fixed original vertex $x$, denote evaluation for the completed fibration by $a$. Choose a section equivalence $e$ from the original section category to the completed section category and an inverse fiber equivalence $w$ from the completed fiber to the original fiber. Step 9 proves weak contractibility of all commas for $a$. The statement of [lem-coef-infinity-cofinal-colimit-restriction] therefore gives weak contractibility of all commas for $v=wae$. The evaluation square and the quasi-inverse data of Step 2 give a coherent natural equivalence from $v$ to the original evaluation $t$. Apply [lem-coef-cofinal-natural-equivalence-invariance] to transfer the comma contractibility from $v$ to $t$. Choose its fixed universe large enough to contain both section categories, fibers and all comparison data. This proves cofinality for the original simplicial base without identifying different strict comma pullbacks by equality.

source.place: HTT 5.4.4.2, transfer back through the opening reduction; natural-equivalence mapping-space argument from returned Step 8 is now a separate input; read online, not archived
